title: Reece Walsh Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week, and understand tax, Medicare, and super. Apply the same method to any hourly wage, including the Reece
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, the annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44/hour yields $52,281.44 annually before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30/hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. This is a gross figure before tax, Medicare, and super.

faqs.q: What tax and Medicare will I pay on my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Use the ATO’s tax tables for an exact estimate.

faqs.q: Does super come out of my salary or is it paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. Your employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary time earnings into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. It is not deducted from your take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you’ve ever wondered how your hourly wage stacks up against an annual salary, you’re not alone. Whether you’re comparing job offers, negotiating a pay rise, or simply curious about the **Reece Walsh salary** figure you’ve seen in the news, the conversion process is straightforward. This guide walks you through the formula, explains tax and super, and shows how to use official pay guides to check your minimum entitlements.

## How to Convert Hourly to Annual

The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a standard full-time week of 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. That gives:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,281.44 per year

If you’re paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by two. For the minimum wage, that’s $1,004.90 per week, or $2,009.80 per fortnight.

## Understanding the Reece Walsh Salary Context

Reece Walsh is a professional rugby league player, and his salary is often reported as an annual figure. While we don’t have his exact hourly rate from the search results, the same conversion method applies in reverse: divide his reported annual salary by 52 and then by 38 to get an equivalent hourly rate. Keep in mind that professional athletes are usually paid annual retainers, not hourly wages, and their contracts may include bonuses and allowances not captured by this simple formula.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Figure

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your tax and Medicare levy using the 2026–27 resident tax scales:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of the excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45% of the excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For the minimum wage example ($52,281.44):

- Tax: $4,020 + 30% × ($52,281.44 – $45,000) = $4,020 + $2,184.43 = $6,204.43
- Medicare: 2% × $52,281.44 = $1,045.63
- Take-home pay: $52,281.44 – $6,204.43 – $1,045.63 = $45,031.38

Note: This estimate uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in our reference. Always check the ATO website for the latest figures.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is not deducted from your salary; it is paid on top by your employer. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For the minimum wage earner:

$52,281.44 × 12% = $6,273.77 added to your super fund each year.

This means your total remuneration (salary plus super) is $58,555.21.

## Using Pay Guides and Award Rates

Many employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates than the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, including penalty rates and allowances. For example, the Health Professionals and Support Services Award and the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Award have specific classifications with their own hourly rates.

If you are a casual worker, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05 per hour (including loading). When using our [timesheet](/), never type a rate that already includes casual loading; instead, check the “casual” box to add it automatically.

To find the correct award for your job, visit the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page or browse the Fair Work Ombudsman’s list of awards.

## Conclusion

Converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is a simple calculation that helps you compare earnings and plan your finances. Remember to use 38 hours per week unless you know your actual hours. Apply the tax and Medicare estimates, and remember that super is paid on top. Whether you’re looking at the **Reece Walsh salary** or your own wage, the same principles apply. For more detailed calculations, refer to the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide or the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page.
